_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list
at run time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
All eleven capacitors on the board are audited and every net was traced on
a Chapter 7 sheet, so source is 'schematic' throughout. There is nothing to
infer: A10 has no regulator of its own, and the four rails it consumes
(+17 S, -17 S, +5 LH, +5 RLH) all arrive at P302 already regulated on A17.
Only three of the eleven are tantalum -- C3, C4 and C6. The other eight are
polyester film (CAP,POLYES,0.22UF,+-5%,50V, stock 747519), which neither
dries out nor fails short the way a tantalum does; they are audited anyway
because the same question is worth asking of every part.
appliedV is the worst case the NODE can reach, not the nominal it normally
sits at. C1 and C3 are the case that matters: their node is U1's positive
supply pin, which sheet 1 feeds from +17 S through VR1, a 3.3 V zener in
series -- so the node normally runs at about +13.7 V. It is recorded at 17 V
because a shorted or shunted VR1 puts the full rail on it and because 17 V
is what it sees at power-up before the zener conducts. Recording 13.7 would
flatter the margin on the strength of one series part.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides what a
shorted part does. These letters are this board's:
A  U1's supply node, from +/-17 S through a small series element (VR1 on
the positive side, R5 100 ohm on the negative). +/-17 S itself is
unfused off A17's 3 A regulators, but nothing here sees the rail
directly: a short would be limited by a 0.4 W zener or a 0.25 W
resistor, both of which open long before the rail notices.
B  +5 RLH, the relay-coil supply, after choke L4. Regulated on A17 and
shared with every relay coil on the board, so a short here stops the
ohms function outright rather than degrading it.
C  +5 LH, the logic supply, after choke L5. Regulated on A17 and shared
with A9's and the motherboard's logic.
Hand-authored; tools/import_cap_audit.py was not used.

C1.net: U1 positive supply node (+17 S through VR1)
C1.note: 0.22 uF polyester, high-frequency bypass in parallel with C3 on U1 pin 7, returned to SCOM. Sheet 1 of 4, inside the dashed GROUND PLANE = SCOM region. Node normally sits about 3.3 V below +17 S because VR1 is in series in the feed.

C2.net: U1 negative supply node (-17 S through R5)
C2.note: 0.22 uF polyester, mirror of C1 on U1 pin 4, returned to SCOM. Sheet 1 of 4. R5 is only 100 ohm and the OPA111 draws a few mA, so this node really does sit at nearly the full -17 S.

C3.net: U1 positive supply node (+17 S through VR1)
C3.note: 10 uF tantalum, 35 V part, the bulk bypass on U1 pin 7 with its + toward the rail. Sheet 1 of 4. One of only three tantalums on the assembly, and with C4 the pair worth looking at first if U1 misbehaves during ohms calibration but the board is otherwise well.

C4.net: U1 negative supply node (-17 S through R5)
C4.note: 10 uF tantalum, 35 V part, the bulk bypass on U1 pin 4 with its + toward SCOM -- correct polarity for a negative rail, and worth checking on a repaired board. Sheet 1 of 4.

C6.note: 4.7 uF tantalum, 25 V part, on the relay-coil supply immediately after choke L4 at P302 pins 23A/23C, returned to RLH COM. Sheet 2 of 4. The only bulk capacitance behind 39 relay coils. CORRECTED 2026-08 from 5.0 V to 6.4 V: the net was traced correctly, but the value had been taken from the rail's name rather than from Table 2-10, which gives +5 RLH as +5.975 V +/-425 mV at A17's TP14. 6.40 V is the top of that band and is what A5, A8, A9, A13, A14, A15 and A17 use for the same rail. 26 % of a 25 V part -- still one of the least stressed tantalums in the instrument, just not the very lowest.

C7.note: 0.22 uF polyester on the logic supply after choke L5 at P302 pins 22A/22C, returned to LH COM. Sheet 2 of 4. The only bypass on +5 LH -- U9, U10 and the VDD pin of all nine 5801 drivers share it.

C10.note: 0.22 uF polyester decoupling U5's COM pin (12) to its GND pin (11), i.e. +5 RLH to RLH COM. Sheet 2 of 4.

C11.note: 0.22 uF polyester decoupling U6, same arrangement as C10. Sheet 2 of 4.

C12.note: 0.22 uF polyester decoupling U11, same arrangement as C10. Sheet 2 of 4.

C13.note: 0.22 uF polyester decoupling U12, same arrangement as C10. Sheet 2 of 4.

C16.note: 0.22 uF polyester decoupling U3, the non-latching driver, same arrangement as C10. Sheet 2 of 4. Five of the nine drivers have their own decoupling cap; U2, U7, U8 and U13 do not.
